{{Short description|Egyptian engineer and editor}}
'''Mohamed El Naschie''' ({{langx|ar|محمد النشائي}}; born 1943)<ref name="self">{{cite web|url=http://www.el-naschie.net|title=el naschie physicist - Engineer|accessdate=January 9, 2020|publisher=Self Published}}</ref> is an Egyptian [[engineer]] and the former editor of the controversial journal ''[[Elsevier#Chaos, Solitons & Fractals|Chaos, Solitons & Fractals]]''. The controversy concerned El Naschie's publication, over many years, of over 300 papers of questioned scientific merit authored by himself with little or no apparent peer review. Published reports of his eventual departure from the journal's editorship led to a lengthy libel court case that raised questions about the libel laws in Great Britain. The controversy has also played a role in discussions of the "[[impact factor]]" as a quality measure for scientific journals and of the methodology of [[university ranking]]s.

==Early life and education==
El Naschie grew up in [[Germany]]. His initial training was as an engineer; he received an engineering degree from [[Leibniz University Hannover]].<ref name="Die Zeit">[http://www.zeit.de/2009/03/N-El-Naschie "Der Felix Krull der Mathematik"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120714074013/http://www.zeit.de/2009/03/N-El-Naschie |date=2012-07-14 }}, ''Die Zeit'' 27 March 2009</ref> He later studied in [[England]] and was awarded a doctorate by the [[University of London]] in 1974, with a thesis entitled "The roll of formulation in elastic buckling" [''sic''].<ref name="ethos">{{cite web|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?did=1&uin=uk.bl.ethos.454723|title=British Library EThOS - search and order theses online |publisher=Ethos.bl.uk |date=2003-11-30 |accessdate=2012-07-07}}</ref>

==Publications==
Between 1974 and 1990 El Naschie published eight papers, mainly relating to the mathematics of [[buckling]], in the ''[[Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics]]''.<ref>[http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/advanced/search Wiley Online Library]</ref> Since then he has published over 400 articles, mainly in the field of theoretical physics, the majority in ''[[Elsevier#Chaos, Solitons & Fractals|Chaos, Solitons & Fractals]]'', a journal of which he was the editor-in-chief, and where standards of [[peer review]] have been questioned.<ref name="SIAM" />

The majority of El Naschie's later publications concern his own controversial ''E-infinity'' theory that the [[universe]] has an infinite number of dimensions and is based on a [[Cantor set|Cantor]] continuum. [[mathematical physics|Mathematical physicist]] professor [[John C. Baez]] of the [[University of California, Riverside]] has called El Naschie's work "undisciplined [[numerology]] filled with impressive [[buzzword]]s",<ref name="Die Zeit" /> while [[cosmologist]] [[Neil Turok]] of the [[Perimeter Institute]], testifying as an [[expert witness]] against El Naschie in a British court case, has strongly criticized the quality of El Naschie's papers, based on criteria such as the occurrence of meaningless or obscure statements, wrong statements, and the lack of any substantial contribution of new knowledge to the field concerned.<ref name="Guardian1" /><ref>Numbers 119 to 160 in {{cite web | url=https://www.nature.com/nature/newspdf/456432a-s1.pdf | title=Judgment : El Nashie v Macmillan Publishers and Schiermeier | date=6 July 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921052632/https://www.nature.com/nature/newspdf/456432a-s1.pdf | accessdate=2012-07-07| archive-date=2013-09-21 }}</ref>
In 2002, El Naschie was awarded a Fellowship by the Frankfurter Förderverein für Physikalische Grundlagenforschung, a private organisation devoted to supporting research, in appreciation of his "original ideas in developing a theory of fractal space-time allowing the determination of the basic constants of nature".<ref name="Judgment">{{cite web | url=https://www.nature.com/nature/newspdf/456432a-s1.pdf | title=Judgment : El Nashie v Macmillan Publishers and Schiermeier | date=6 July 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921052632/https://www.nature.com/nature/newspdf/456432a-s1.pdf | accessdate=2012-07-07| archive-date=2013-09-21 }}</ref>

==''Chaos, Solitons & Fractals''==
{{See also|Elsevier#Chaos, Solitons & Fractals|l1=Chaos, Solitons & Fractals}}
At the end of the 1980s, [[chaos theory]] and [[fractal]] [[mathematics]] were in fashion, and El Naschie wished to apply these concepts to engineering.<ref name="Die Zeit" /> In 1991 El Naschie founded the scientific journal ''Chaos, Solitons & Fractals'',<ref name="Nature">{{Cite journal | journal = Nature | date = 26 November 2008 | title = Self-publishing editor set to retire | volume = 456 | issue = 7221 | page =432 | doi = 10.1038/456432a | pmid=19037282 | last1 = Schiermeier | first1 = Q| doi-access = free }}</ref> initially with the [[United Kingdom|British]] publisher [[Pergamon Press]].<ref name="Die Zeit" /> When Pergamon was sold, the journal passed to the [[Elsevier]] stable.<ref name="Die Zeit" /> He served as its editor-in- hief until his retirement in 2009.<ref name="Nature"/> El Naschie published over 300 of his own papers in the journal, and this extremely high rate of self-publication by the editor-in-chief led to charges that normal standards of peer review were not upheld at the journal.<ref name="SIAM">{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=1663|title=Integrity Under Attack: The State of Scholarly Publishing|date=4 December 2009|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829211352/http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=1663|archivedate=29 August 2017|accessdate=9 December 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Peter Woit]] of [[Columbia University]] was quoted as saying "it's plain obvious that there was either zero, or at best very poor, peer review, of his own papers".<ref name="Nature" /> El Naschie has said "Senior people are above this childish, vain practice of peer review."<ref name="NewSci">{{cite web|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn21169-el-naschie-questions-journalist-in-nature-libel-trial.html |title=El Naschie questions journalist in Nature libel trial |date=16 November 2011|accessdate=7 July 2012}}</ref> [[Otto Rössler]], an honorary editor of the journal and a biochemist best known for his involvement in a failed lawsuit to halt the [[Large Hadron Collider]] due to fears that it would generate mini black holes, stated in British court testimony that "if you have something new to offer, peer review is dangerous" and "delays progress in science".<ref>{{citation|title=Nature journal libel case continues|first=Pallab|last=Ghosh|journal=[[BBC News]]|date=25 November 2011|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-15889634}}.</ref> The journal also had a high level of self-citation, which increased its [[impact factor]].<ref name="Nature"/>

==''Nature'' libel case==
In 2008, the journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' published a news article by Quirin Schiermeier alleging that some of El Naschie's papers did not appear to be properly peer-reviewed and that he claimed institutional affiliations that could not be confirmed.<ref name="Guardian1">[https://www.theguardian.com/science/2011/nov/18/nature-libel-trial "Nature magazine accused of libel"], ''The Guardian'' 18 November 2011</ref> El Naschie disputed these allegations and sued ''Nature'' for libel. In July 2012 the case was dismissed, with the judge ruling that the article was "substantially true", contained "honest comment" and was "the product of responsible journalism". The judgement noted that El Naschie, who represented himself in court, had failed to provide any documentary evidence that his papers had been peer-reviewed.<ref name="Guardian2">[https://www.theguardian.com/science/2012/jul/06/nature-libel-peer-review?newsfeed=true "Nature libel verdict 'a victory for free speech'"],''The Guardian'' 6 July 2012</ref>
Judge [[Victoria Sharp]] also found "reasonable and serious grounds" for suspecting that El Naschie used a range of false names to defend his editorial practice in communications with ''Nature'' and described this behavior as "curious" and "bizarre".<ref>{{cite magazine
| last        = Aron
| first       = Jacob
| date        = 6 July 2012
| title       = Nature Publishing Group wins libel trial
|magazine= New Scientist
| issue       = 2873
| url         = https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn22026-nature-publishing-group-wins-libel-trial.html
| accessdate  = 14 July 2012
}}</ref>

==University ranking controversy==

El Naschie's practice of publishing a great number of articles in a journal of which he himself was the editor also came to public attention when it was identified as a crucial contributing factor for propelling [[Alexandria University]] into the top group of the ''[[Times Higher Education]]'' magazine's university rankings. This evidence of such rankings being easily skewed has led to criticism of the methodology of university rankings in general.<ref name="NYTimes1">[https://www.nytimes.com/2010/11/15/education/15iht-educLede15.html Questionable Science Behind Academic Rankings], ''The New York Times'' 14 November 2010.</ref>
